orientation: PR-2 introduces customer-to-customer payment functionality between accounts in the same currency. It adds the Payments domain model, EF Core configuration, PaymentService with daily limit enforcement and idempotency handling, along with PaymentsController endpoints. The changes aim to satisfy requirement PR-2 for secure money transfers within customer limits.

findings.title: Composite index on CustomerId and IdempotencyKey is not configured as unique
findings.claim: The EF Core index on Payment (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) lacks .IsUnique(). Without a unique constraint at the database level, duplicate payment records can be persisted and DbUpdateException will not be raised during concurrent duplicate requests.
findings.requirement_link: Two simultaneous requests with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey could both pass an application-level existence check and trigger duplicate ledger transfers unless enforced by a unique database constraint on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey).
findings.suggested_fix: Chain .IsUnique() to the index configuration: modelBuilder.Entity<Payment>().HasIndex(p => new { p.CustomerId, p.IdempotencyKey }).IsUnique();

findings.title: Missing idempotency check prior to daily limit calculation and ledger posting
findings.claim: PayAsync does not check whether a payment with (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) already exists before checking the daily transfer limit and calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync. As a result, retried requests with an existing key can fail daily limit checks or move money again via the ledger instead of returning the existing payment without ledger calls.
findings.requirement_link: Calling PayAsync with an IdempotencyKey already used by the same CustomerId returns the existing Payment record without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync, without counting the amount again toward the daily limit, and without publishing another PaymentCompleted event; identical IdempotencyKey values from different customers are treated independently.
findings.suggested_fix: Query _db.Payments for an existing payment matching customerId and request.IdempotencyKey at the beginning of PayAsync. If found, return it immediately before evaluating daily transfer limits or posting transfers to ILedger.

findings.title: Idempotency database index lacks unique constraint
findings.claim: The composite index on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) is created without uniqueness. Without a unique constraint, concurrent identical requests are not prevented at the database level, allowing duplicate payment records and failing to trigger unique violation handling.
findings.requirement_link: Two simultaneous requests with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey could both pass an application-level existence check and trigger duplicate ledger transfers unless enforced by a unique database constraint on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey).
findings.suggested_fix: Chain .IsUnique() to the index configuration in BankDbContext.OnModelCreating.

findings.title: Idempotency check is bypassed before money movement in ledger
findings.claim: PaymentService invokes ILedger.PostTransferAsync before checking if a payment with the specified IdempotencyKey already exists for the customer. This causes duplicate money transfers when requests are retried with the same idempotency key.
findings.requirement_link: Calling PayAsync with an IdempotencyKey already used by the same CustomerId returns the existing Payment record without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync, without counting the amount again toward the daily limit, and without publishing another PaymentCompleted event; identical IdempotencyKey values from different customers are treated independently.
findings.suggested_fix: Query _db.Payments for an existing payment matching CustomerId and request.IdempotencyKey before calculating daily limits and before calling _ledger.PostTransferAsync; return the existing record if found.
findings.drop_reason: Capped at Major: a architecture finding is never Critical on its own

findings.title: In-memory materialization of daily payment amounts causes unnecessary allocations
findings.claim: PayAsync calls ToListAsync on lines 94-100 to materialize all completed payment amounts for the day into an in-memory List<decimal> before summing them via LINQ. This transfers all individual amount records over the database connection and allocates a list on every payment rather than computing the sum directly on the database server.
findings.requirement_link: Before moving money, PayAsync sums the CustomerId's completed payments whose CreatedAt falls within the current UTC calendar day (using IClock.UtcNow); if that sum plus request.Amount exceeds BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit, PayAsync throws DailyLimitExceededException and does not move money or persist a Payment, whereas a total exactly equal to BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit is permitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Use EF Core's SumAsync directly on the filtered IQueryable (e.g., await _db.Payments.Where(...).SumAsync(p => (decimal?)p.Amount, ct) ?? 0m) to execute an SQL SUM aggregate.

findings.title: Unconditional ledger transfer execution causes repeated redundant work on retried idempotency keys
findings.claim: PayAsync executes ILedger.PostTransferAsync before checking if a payment record with the given CustomerId and IdempotencyKey already exists. Retrying a request with the same idempotency key executes redundant ledger transfers and database operations rather than short-circuiting early.
findings.requirement_link: Calling PayAsync with an IdempotencyKey already used by the same CustomerId returns the existing Payment record without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync, without counting the amount again toward the daily limit, and without publishing another PaymentCompleted event; identical IdempotencyKey values from different customers are treated independently.
findings.suggested_fix: Query BankDbContext.Payments for an existing record with the matching CustomerId and IdempotencyKey before initiating the daily limit check or ledger transfer, returning the existing payment immediately if found.
findings.drop_reason: Capped at Major: a performance finding is never Critical on its own

findings.title: Missing AsNoTracking in customer payment history query creates unnecessary change tracker overhead
findings.claim: ForCustomerAsync queries customer payments for read-only consumption without applying AsNoTracking(). Materializing entities into EF Core's ChangeTracker allocates identity tracking structures for records that are mapped directly to DTOs and never updated in the current DbContext scope.
findings.requirement_link: GET api/payments calls IPaymentService.ForCustomerAsync with ICurrentUser.UserId and returns only the authenticated customer's Payment records.
findings.suggested_fix: Add .AsNoTracking() to the query pipeline in ForCustomerAsync.

findings.title: No unit or integration tests for PaymentsController endpoints
findings.claim: PaymentsController defines POST and GET api/payments with authorization and exception-to-HTTP mapping, but neither the controller nor its endpoints are exercised in tests. Crucial behaviors like Customer policy enforcement and status code mapping remain unverified.
findings.requirement_link: Both POST api/payments and GET api/payments require the Customer policy (Policies.Customer), and PaymentService always identifies the caller using ICurrentUser.UserId rather than any user identifier from a request payload or query parameter.
findings.suggested_fix: Add controller tests to verify authorization attributes, customer ID resolution from ICurrentUser, and mapping of domain exceptions (e.g., UnauthorizedAccessException to 403, DailyLimitExceededException to 409).
